meta: Artemisia Gentileschi's earliest signed and dated work, Susanna and the Elders of 1610, in Pommersfelden.
about: Susanna and the Elders of 1610 is Artemisia Gentileschi's earliest known signed and dated work. A frightened Susanna is accosted by two men above her as she bathes, a popular subject in the Baroque. The elders demanded favors, she refused, and they then falsely accused her of adultery, a crime punishable by death, until Daniel proved her innocence. Artemisia painted several versions in her career, and this one hangs at Schloss Weißenstein in Pommersfelden.

meta: A winged fantastic bird framed by rocaille with three men, a chinoiserie print by François-Thomas Mondon, about 1730.
about: This chinoiserie ornament print shows figures and fantastical birds. In the center is a winged fantastical bird, framed by rocaille ornament with three male figures around it, and another bird on top of the ornament looks down at it. The ornament uses C-scrolls, shells, feathers, bat wings, scrolling leaves and festoons of flowers. François-Thomas Mondon made the print around 1730.

meta: A smiling young woman leans on a stone balustrade beside a bundle with a wine bottle, a study by Jan Adam Kruseman, 1827.
about: This is a study of a young woman, smiling and leaning forward with her arms on a stone balustrade. At the right is a bundle knotted in a cloth with a bottle of wine. Jan Adam Kruseman painted it in 1827.

meta: A shepherd with a flock of sheep in a Drenthe landscape with a few trees, painted by Alphonse Stengelin in 1875.
about: In this landscape in Drenthe, a shepherd tends a flock of sheep among a few trees. Alphonse Stengelin painted it in 1875, and the Rijksmuseum holds it. Its note describes only the shepherd and the flock.

meta: An auricular-style ewer design with mermaids, a dolphin and a dragon on the spout, by Jan Lutma, about 1630.
about: This is a design for an ewer in the auricular style. A mermaid is intertwined with the dolphin's tail at the lower outside of the handle, and a dragon stands on the spout. Neptune is shown alone, and a kneeling mermaid is at the shaft. Jan Lutma made the design around 1630.

meta: Moretto da Brescia's Lament over the Dead Christ, painted between 1526 and 1530 and now in the National Gallery of Art.
about: Moretto da Brescia painted this Lament over the Dead Christ between 1526 and 1530, late in his youth. Wikipedia says it closely resembles the central panel of Paolo Caylina the Younger's Deposition Altarpiece from the same years, though the colors are brighter and clearer. Moretto reused some of its elements later in his career. It is now in the National Gallery of Art in Washington.

meta: Apollo and Calliope make music in a hilly landscape by Abraham Genoels, about 1685, a pendant picture.
about: A hilly landscape with Apollo and Calliope has a flowing stream in the foreground and sheep at the right. Abraham Genoels painted it in 1685 as a pendant to another picture in the Rijksmuseum.

meta: Leonardo's portrait of Ginevra de' Benci, painted in Florence between 1474 and 1478, now the only Leonardo on public view in the Americas.
about: Leonardo painted this portrait in Florence between 1474 and 1478, perhaps for Ginevra's marriage or, more likely, her engagement, since wedding portraits were made in pairs and she faces right. A juniper bush surrounds her head, a symbol of female virtue that also puns on her name, since the Italian for juniper is ginepro. On the back a juniper sprig in a wreath carries the motto Beauty adorns virtue. The National Gallery of Art bought it from the Prince of Liechtenstein in 1967.

meta: A design for a table clock with fluted pilasters, a laurel garland and a covered urn, by Richard de Lalonde, about 1770.
about: Two fluted pilasters flank the circular dial of this table clock design. Above it a pediment carries a covered urn on top, a garland of laurel leaves, and a shell in the recessed part. A trophy decorated with leaves and a bow is in the lower panel. Partial views of covered urns stand on either side of the base, which has cushioned feet. Richard de Lalonde made the design around 1770.

meta: Luca Signorelli's Madonna and Child with Saints, painted about 1519 to 1523 for the Brotherhood of Saint Jerome in Arezzo.
about: Luca Signorelli painted this Madonna with Child and Saints around 1519 to 1523. It is a traditional Holy Conversation composition. The Brotherhood of Saint Jerome in Arezzo ordered it for their seat. He made it in Cortona and brought it to Arezzo himself, when he was in his seventies. It is now in the Museo nazionale d'arte medievale e moderna in Arezzo.

meta: A woman works in the kitchen of a farmhouse barn with a girl watching, painted by Egbert van der Poel in 1646.
about: This is the interior of a farmhouse barn, with a woman at work in the kitchen and a girl watching. Pots and household goods are set out in the foreground, with fowl and vegetables in a basket. A grindstone stands at the left foreground, and a woman milks a goat in the background. Egbert Lievensz. van der Poel painted it in 1646.

meta: Karl Hofer's The Letter of 1934, from an artist the Nazis condemned as degenerate and whose studio was bombed in 1943.
about: Hofer's art is full of disillusionment and pessimism and expresses his dark view of modern life through a narrow range of themes he repeated obsessively. He was born in Karlsruhe and settled in Berlin in 1913. The Nazis condemned him as a degenerate artist and dismissed him from his teaching post in 1933. In 1943 his studio and most of his work were destroyed by bombing. He painted The Letter in 1934.

meta: Two geese fly out to sea in Maruyama Okyo's painting from sliding doors, about 1800.
about: Two geese fly out to sea in this painting that was once mounted on four sliding doors between two rooms. Geese stand for autumn in Japanese and Chinese painting and poetry, and their yearly migrations also stand for an unsettled life. The museum says the dramatic, spacious realism comes from Okyo's study of European art, where he learned some ways of showing perspective and volume.

meta: A landscape in the style of Ni Zan from Chen Hongshou's double album of twenty paintings after ancient masters.
about: The twenty paintings in this double album by Chen Hongshou include landscapes and figures as well as flowers, and one leaf with a woman, a subject not found in the other albums of his later career. The museum calls his late works summations of his peculiar and quirky art, archaistic and hyper-refined but without shallowness or sentimentality. His figures and landscapes in these late albums are miniaturized, like small Chinese gardens. This leaf is a landscape in the style of Ni Zan.

meta: A pile of skulls under carrion birds outside a Central Asian city in Vasily Vereshchagin's The Apotheosis of War, 1871.
about: A heap of human skulls lies on barren ground, the aftermath of a battle or siege, and a flock of carrion birds picks over it. Vasily Vereshchagin painted it in 1871 in Munich, as one of thirteen works about his earlier travels with the Russian army in Central Asia, and dedicated it to all great conquerors, past, present and to come. It belongs to his Turkestan Series and is in the Tretyakov Gallery in Moscow.

meta: Edward H. Potthast's In the Surf, about 1910, from his summers on the New England coast.
about: Edward Potthast was born in Cincinnati and studied in Munich and Paris before returning to the United States, where he began spending summers on the New England coast. There he studied the carefree seaside activities of bathers and picnickers. He never married but was especially fond of painting young mothers and their children.
credit_line: Gift of Virginia Rose Glidden and family and Mr. and Mrs. William H. Marlatt Fund

meta: A pleasure boat on the Sumida River heads for the Yoshiwara by the San'ya Canal in Teisai Hokuba's painting of the 1800s.
about: After a major fire in Edo, the Yoshiwara licensed brothel district was moved to an area reached by boat on the Sumida River, which produced many pictures of the trip. Here attendants in checkered robes serve refreshment to a client, a figure at the front of the boat tends the kitchen, and a courtesan at the back looks over the river. Acquaintances talk in small commuter boats, and fishers put in at a tiny island. Teisai Hokuba painted it.
credit_line: The Kelvin Smith Collection, given by Mrs. Kelvin Smith

meta: Félix Vallotton's Corn Fields of 1900, painted after he turned from printmaking to oil, with blurred greenery and a simple horizon.
about: Around 1900 Vallotton shifted from printmaking to oil painting. Before then he concentrated on reproducing the world around him precisely, but as this painting shows, his work now has hints of ambiguity. The greenery blends together, and the far horizon is described by simple curves of hills or clouds fading into the sky.
credit_line: Nancy F. and Joseph P. Keithley Collection Gift
